title: Consent-led Network Change Ledger - PRD (WIP)
body:
Goal
Create a lightweight, customer-facing PRD for an auditable, consent-driven network change ledger that harmonizes approval gates, tamper-evident audit logs, and customer-managed networking workflows. This is aimed at on-prem / VPC customers who require explicit consent, verifiable evidence bundles, and deterministic rollback points for network/operator-initiated changes.

Context and motivation
- Problem: customers on Private deployments ask for stronger guarantees that network changes (firewall, peering, NAT, route tables, operator bundles) are authorized, auditable, and reversible. Current docs focus on approval flows but lack a compact evidence model and sampling rules for audits.
- Opportunity: provide a formal ledger concept that ties approval records, operator attestations, syscall/agent logs, and optional customer-signed consent tokens into a single change artifact. This reduces dispute resolution time and simplifies compliance evidence collection.

High level product idea
- A Change Ledger is a sequence of immutable change records stored in the customer’s tenancy (optionally mirrored to Redwood for SLA-bound customers). Each record contains: change metadata, approval checkpoint(s), operator attestation, optional customer-signed consent blob, and a forensics pointer (bundle id or S3 path).
- Approval gates map to checkpoint types: pre-approve, canary, full-rollout, emergency-rollback. Each checkpoint has required approvers (customer admin, operator on-call, compliance reviewer) and a minimum evidence set.
- Audit sampling: immutable ledger entries are eligible for sampled evidence snapshots (configurable rate + SLO-driven overrides). Snapshots are bundled into tamper-evident artifacts for retention and audit export.

User stories
- As a network admin, I want to request a firewall rule change and capture an approval chain I can export for auditors.
- As a compliance officer, I want to randomly sample 1% of changes and receive full evidence bundles for retention.
- As an SRE operator, I want emergency rollback to bypass full approvals but still emit an emergency attestation entry that explains rationale and links to post-mortem.

Requirements (MUST/HIGH/MED/LOW)
- MUST: Ledger entries are append-only and cryptographically timestamped (HSM/KMS-backed signing).
- MUST: Store references to the minimal evidence set for each checkpoint (approver id, ticket id, operator attestation text, binary evidence pointer).
- MUST: Support configurable approval presets per-customer (e.g., 2-admins OR 1-admin + compliance).
- HIGH: Provide an exportable audit bundle format (zip with manifest.json + sha256 checksums).
- HIGH: Allow customer-managed storage endpoints for evidence bundles (S3-compatible) or Redwood-managed storage with retention controls.
- MED: Integrate with customer ticketing (Jira/ServiceNow) to auto-populate the change reason and link.
- LOW: Optional customer-side SDK to sign consent tokens before changes are executed.

Design notes and data model (sketch)
- ChangeRecord (manifest fields as text in ledger): id, timestamp, actor, change_type, target_resources, approval_state, evidence_refs[], attestation_signatures[], previous_record_id.
- Evidence bundle: manifest.json, logs.tar.gz (agent logs), config-diff.patch, screenshots/diagrams optional, approvals.csv (who/when/what).
- Retention policy: per-customer policy with min 90d up to 7y for regulated customers.

Approval gate presets (examples)
- Low-risk presets: 1-admin approval auto-apply after 2h if no objection.
- Standard: 2-admin approval or 1-admin + compliance signoff. Canary flow attaches canary-observation snapshot to ledger entry.
- Emergency: operator attestation + automated post-hoc workflow that requires full evidence bundle within 48h.

Operational considerations
- Performance: ledger writes must not add >150ms median latency to API-driven change requests (write is async with sync-ack pattern).
- Storage: metadata (manifests) kept in WAL DB (encrypted), evidence bundles stored in blob store. Provide TTL and retention lifecycles.
- Security: sign manifests with tenant KMS key when available; fallback to Redwood-signing with customer key escrow. All URIs to evidence bundles must be signed URLs.
- Privacy: redact PII from logs by default; offer opt-in raw logs with explicit consent.

Forensics & Investigation flow
- Investigator pulls a ChangeRecord -> clicks evidence bundle link -> downloads zips that include manifest + logs + diffs.
- If signed consent token exists, verify signature against customer public key. If missing, follow escalation playbook.

API contract (outline)
- POST /v1/private/change-requests -> returns change_id, ledger_write_status (queued/synced). Payload includes desired change, ticket refs, approver list.
- GET /v1/private/changes/{id} -> returns manifest with approval chain and evidence_refs.
- POST /v1/private/changes/{id}/attest -> operator/customer attestation blob (signed).
- GET /v1/private/changes/{id}/audit-export -> triggers async bundle creation and returns signed URL.

Edge cases and open questions
- How do we handle multi-tenant operator runbooks that affect multiple customer ledgers? (suggest separate multi-record coordinated commit with cross-references).
- Legal: are customer-signed tokens legally sufficient in every region? Pass to legal.
- Cost model: should audit exports be metered separately? Map to billing team.
- Disaster recovery: what is required to reconstruct ledger state if bucket is lost? Need local index + redundant mirrors.

Implementation plan (high level phases)
- Phase 0 (research): interviews with 3 large customers, SRE + compliance workshops. (owner: Maya)
- Phase 1 (proto): implement manifest + WAL DB writes, simple approvals, Redwood-managed evidence storage, export format (4 weeks).
- Phase 2 (customer opt-in): storage connectors to S3-compatible endpoints, KMS integration for tenant signing, retention UI changes (6 weeks).
- Phase 3 (hardening): sampling pipeline for audit retention, cross-tenant coordinated commits, performance SLAs (8 weeks).

Acceptance criteria
- End-to-end sample change recorded -> evidence bundle exportable -> SHA256 manifest verification passes in audit test.
- RBAC: only approvers in preset can move approval_state to approved.
- Retention policy enforcement: deleted bundles are inaccessible post-TTL from Redwood-managed storage.

Open TODOs (small, actionable)
- [ ] Add sketch of manifest.json schema with exact fields and examples (owner: Owen)
- [ ] Legal feasibility check for signed consent token (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Cost estimate for storage/exports for mid-market vs enterprise (owner: Daniel)
- [ ] Wireframe for Console export UI (owner: Lina)

Quick notes / rough checklist for interviews
- Ask customers about their existing evidence bundles and what format auditors accept (CSV? PDFs?)
- Which ticket ID formats do they want surfaced automatically? (Jira key vs internal id)
- Will they want a read-only mirror of ledger in their own S3?

References / related docs
- product/private-deployments/operator-attestation-onboarding-prd-sketch (drive)
- product/private-deployments/customer-edge-forensics-protocol (drive)
- Jira RDW-2345 (change ledger epic)

Slack snippets (copied rough)
- @ops: "we need a defensible audit artifact for oncall emergency changes — can we require post-hoc evidence within 24h?"
- @legal: "signed tokens sound neat but need to confirm region-by-region acceptance. linking CONF page"

This file is intentionally sketchy — aims to capture the product framing and next steps for proto implementation. Will follow up with manifest schema and a tiny PoC that records 10 test changes (local dev cluster) for verification.
